objects.description: C++ smart-pointer deleter functor compatible with std::unique_ptr<void, MEM_freeN_smart_ptr_deleter>. Calls MEM_freeN and nulls the pointer via MEM_SAFE_FREE. Use it as a custom deleter for memory allocated by MEM_* C API when managing it with unique_ptr.

functions.name: MEM_allocN_len
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the memory block pointed to by vmemh, assuming it was allocated by the guarded allocator in this module. Intended for debugging/accounting of allocations.
requirements: vmemh must be a pointer to memory previously allocated by this module; otherwise behavior is undefined
Return value is the size of the originally requested allocation (not including allocator overhead)

functions.name: MEM_freeN
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by the C-style MEM_* allocation functions of this module. Illegal to use for objects created with the C++ MEM_new/MEM_delete API.
requirements: vmemh must be a pointer obtained from the C-style MEM_* allocation functions from this module (e.g., MEM_mallocN, MEM_callocN, MEM_reallocN_id, etc.)
Do not pass pointers allocated with MEM_new or C++ operator new overloads using this backend; use MEM_delete instead for those
Passing NULL is allowed implicitly by common patterns but not explicitly documented here

functions.name: MEM_dupallocN
functions.description: Duplicates a memory block and returns a pointer to a newly allocated copy. NULL-safe: returns NULL when vmemh is NULL. Typically used to copy blocks managed by this allocator.
requirements: vmemh should be a pointer to memory allocated by this module (so its size is known) or NULL
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN
If vmemh is NULL, function returns NULL

functions.name: MEM_reallocN_id
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_reallocN_id)(void *vmemh, size_t len, const char *str);
functions.description: Reallocates a memory block to a new size len, returning a pointer to the new block and freeing the old one. Not a system realloc; it allocates new memory and copies the contents.
requirements: vmemh must be a pointer to a block allocated by this module
len is the new requested size in bytes
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
On failure may return NULL; the old block semantics are not documented here—callers should handle NULL safely

functions.name: MEM_recallocN_id
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_recallocN_id)(void *vmemh, size_t len, const char *str);
functions.description: Reallocates a block to size len like MEM_reallocN_id but zero-initializes any newly added bytes.
requirements: vmemh must be a pointer to a block allocated by this module
len is the new requested size in bytes
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)

functions.name: MEM_callocN
functions.description: Allocates a zero-initialized memory block of size len bytes with a static tag name str for debugging/accounting.
requirements: len is the requested size in bytes
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_calloc_arrayN
functions.signature: void *MEM_calloc_arrayN(size_t len, size_t size, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates a zero-initialized array of len elements of element size size. Aborts on integer overflow of len*size to prevent vulnerabilities. str is a static tag name.
requirements: len is the number of elements
size is the size of each element in bytes
The product len*size is checked and the allocator will abort on overflow
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_mallocN
functions.description: Allocates an uninitialized memory block of size len bytes with a static tag name str.
requirements: len is the requested size in bytes
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_malloc_arrayN
functions.signature: void *MEM_malloc_arrayN(size_t len, size_t size, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates an uninitialized array of len elements of size size. Aborts on integer overflow of len*size. str is a static tag name.
requirements: len is the number of elements
size is the size of each element in bytes
The product len*size is checked and the allocator will abort on overflow
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_mallocN_aligned
functions.signature: void *MEM_mallocN_aligned(size_t len, size_t alignment, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates an uninitialized memory block of size len bytes aligned to alignment with a static tag name str.
requirements: len is the requested size in bytes
alignment is the requested alignment in bytes (exact constraints are not documented here)
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_malloc_arrayN_aligned
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_malloc_arrayN_aligned)(size_t len, size_t size, size_t alignment, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates an uninitialized array of len elements of size size with the specified alignment. str is a static tag name.
requirements: len is the number of elements
size is the size of each element in bytes
alignment is the requested alignment in bytes (exact constraints are not documented here)
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_calloc_arrayN_aligned
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_calloc_arrayN_aligned)(size_t len, size_t size, size_t alignment, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates a zero-initialized array of len elements of size size with the specified alignment. str is a static tag name.
requirements: len is the number of elements
size is the size of each element in bytes
alignment is the requested alignment in bytes (exact constraints are not documented here)
str must be a static string (only the pointer is stored)
Returned memory must be freed with MEM_freeN

functions.name: MEM_printmemlist_pydict
functions.description: Prints a list of currently allocated memory blocks as a Python dict format for easier investigation.
requirements: Callable only in environments where stdout/stderr output is available
Intended for debugging/inspection; has no return value

functions.name: MEM_printmemlist
functions.description: Prints a list of the names and sizes of all currently allocated memory blocks.
requirements: Callable only in environments where output is available
Intended for debugging/inspection; has no return value

functions.name: MEM_callbackmemlist
functions.description: Invokes the provided callback func for every allocated memory block.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer taking a single void* argument
func should be reentrant and safe to call for allocator-managed pointers; further constraints are not documented

functions.name: MEM_printmemlist_stats
functions.description: Prints statistics about memory usage maintained by the guarded allocator.
requirements: Callable only in environments where output is available
Intended for debugging/inspection; has no return value

functions.name: MEM_set_error_callback
functions.description: Sets the callback function used by the allocator to report error messages.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer taking a const char* message
Callback may be invoked from allocator error paths; avoid heavy or non-reentrant behavior (not explicitly documented)

functions.name: MEM_consistency_check
functions.description: Checks whether start/end block markers for all tracked allocations are intact.
requirements: Returns true if all memory is consistent; false if corruption is detected
Pure check; does not modify allocations

functions.name: MEM_set_memory_debug
functions.description: Attempts to enforce platform behavior where malloc and stack memory are non-zeroed (e.g., on macOS). Debug aid.
requirements: Has no parameters or return; effect is platform-specific

functions.name: MEM_get_memory_in_use
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes currently in use by allocations tracked by the allocator.
requirements: None beyond allocator initialization

functions.name: MEM_get_memory_blocks_in_use
functions.description: Returns the number of currently allocated memory blocks tracked by the allocator.
requirements: None beyond allocator initialization

functions.name: MEM_reset_peak_memory
functions.description: Resets the tracked peak memory usage statistic to zero.
requirements: Affects allocator’s internal statistics only

functions.name: MEM_get_peak_memory
functions.description: Returns the peak memory usage in bytes observed so far, including mmap allocations.
requirements: None beyond allocator initialization

functions.name: MEM_name_ptr
functions.description: Returns the debugging name/string associated with the allocated block at vmemh. Only available in non-release (NDEBUG not defined) builds.
requirements: vmemh must be a pointer to memory allocated by the guarded allocator
This API is only available when NDEBUG is not defined (debug builds)

functions.name: MEM_name_ptr_set
functions.description: Changes the debugging name/string for the memory allocated at vmemh. Helps make leak reports more specific. Only affects the guarded allocator and only available in debug builds.
requirements: vmemh must be a pointer to memory allocated by the guarded allocator
str must be a non-null static string (only a pointer is stored)
Available only when NDEBUG is not defined (debug builds)

functions.name: MEM_init_memleak_detection
functions.description: Initializes memory leak detection. After calling, information about memory leaks will be printed on process exit.
requirements: Should be called as early as possible in program startup to catch all leaks

functions.name: MEM_enable_fail_on_memleak
functions.description: Configures the process to exit with a failure status code if memory leaks are detected on shutdown. Useful for automated tests.
requirements: Call after MEM_init_memleak_detection to have effect on the leak detection run at exit

functions.name: MEM_use_lockfree_allocator
functions.description: Switches allocator to a faster, less-tracked lock-free mode (tracks counts/bytes, not names). Intended for production performance.
requirements: Must be called before any allocation has occurred
Once allocations have been made, switching allocator types is not allowed

functions.name: MEM_use_guarded_allocator
functions.description: Switches allocator to the slow, fully guarded mode with locks around allocator calls and full block list tracking. Intended for debugging.
requirements: Must be called before any allocation has occurred
Once allocations have been made, switching allocator types is not allowed

functions.name: MEM_construct_leak_detection_data
functions.description: Constructs an object of type T and registers it so it will only be destructed after leak detection has run. Thread-safe. Intended for long-lived process-global or thread-local state that must outlive leak checks.
requirements: T must be constructible from Args...
The returned object should not own any memory allocated with MEM_* functions, otherwise those allocations will be reported as leaked
Calling code should typically store the reference/pointer in static thread_local storage or otherwise synchronize access to prevent concurrent races
